correctness.rationale: The construction is correct over every finite field. For the quadratic extension K/F with nontrivial automorphism sigma, T=L_a sigma satisfies T^2=N(a)I and is nonscalar for a nonzero a. Cayley--Hamilton then forces tr(T)=0, while T is invertible whenever a is nonzero. Thus U={L_a sigma} is a two-dimensional trace-zero subspace with no nonzero nilpotents. Adding any trace-one matrix E gives a direct three-dimensional space W. A nilpotent u+cE has trace zero, hence c=0, and the remaining u is either zero or invertible. Characteristic two causes no exception because trace and Cayley--Hamilton retain these identities.
